study.title: Gender-related difference in altered fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations after electroacupuncture on primary insomnia patients: A resting-state fMRI study
study.study_design: Clinical trial with resting-state fMRI; within-subject pre-post design with gender-stratified comparison
study.population: Primary insomnia patients from outpatient clinic
study.inclusion_criteria: (a) patients aged from 18 to 65 years old; (b) patients with sleep onset latency or wake after sleep onset of >30 min at least 3 nights per week, with symptoms lasting for ≥3 months; (c) patients with a Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI) score of >7 and Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS) score of ≥6
study.exclusion_criteria: (a) patients with uncontrolled medical or psychiatric conditions; (b) patients with the self-rating anxiety scale (SAS) or self-rating depression scale (SDS) score of ≥50; (c) patients diagnosed with comorbid sleep disorders, such as obstructive sleep apnea; (d) patients with alcohol and/or other drug abuse or dependence; (e) patients who received hypnotic or sedating medications or accepted electroacupuncture treatment in the recent 1 month

extraction_notes.note: No sham or placebo control arm is included; all participants received verum electroacupuncture. There is no active comparator. The study design is pre-post within-subject with between-gender comparison only.

MASS (Massachusetts General Hospital acupuncture sensation scale) was used to screen and rate De-Qi sensations, but no quantitative MASS subscale scores are reported in the paper. Only the list of sensations assessed (soreness, numbness, heaviness, warmth, coldness, sharp pain, dull pain) is provided.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures were not assessed or reported. No information on whether patients were naive to acupuncture or held prior expectations.

The abstract states the decreased PSQI was significantly more in FPIs than MPIs with p < .05, while Table 1 reports p = .023 for PSQI-decrease and p = .005 for PSQI-post between groups. These reflect different comparisons (change score vs. post-treatment value). Both are preserved separately in clinical outcomes.

Table 2 (gender difference at baseline): The row labeled 'Precuneus / Posterior cingulate' with BA 31 is listed as a single cluster with coordinates −6, −66, 27. The table uses 'Precuneus' and 'Posterior cingulate' as two labels for the same row; both are preserved in the region label.

Table 4 (FPIs post-treatment): The row for 'Inferior frontal gyrus / Middle frontal gyrus' is listed as a single cluster entry at coordinates −51, 12, 24 with cluster size 33. Both region names are preserved.
Table 3 (MPIs post-treatment): No Brodmann area is reported for Medial frontal gyrus, Superior parietal lobule, Postcentral gyrus (bilateral). These are marked as 'not_reported' accordingly.
No information about adverse events is reported beyond the safety monitoring protocol statement. It is unclear whether any adverse events occurred.

The paper reports a significant age difference between FPIs (52.88 ± 4.55 years) and MPIs (45.00 ± 12.70 years) at baseline (p = .022). Age was not reported as a covariate in the fMRI analyses, which is a potential confound not discussed in the paper.
Flip angle (FA) for T1 sequence is not reported. FA for rs-fMRI is reported as 90°. FOV for T1 is 256 × 256 mm; for rs-fMRI is 106 × 106 mm. Slice thickness and gap are not reported.
The paper states ALFF was also calculated but results are only reported for fALFF. ALFF results are not presented in the results section.
The voxel sizes reported (T1: 1 × 1; rs-fMRI: 2.4 × 2.4) appear to be missing the third dimension in the PDF text. Resampled voxel size for analysis is reported as 3 × 3 × 3 mm³.

The paper does not specify whether white matter and CSF signals were regressed as nuisance regressors separate from or together with head motion parameters; the text states 'nuisance linear regression (including the white matter, the cerebrospinal fluid and head motion parameters)'.

The Table 9 (Table 2 in paper, gender difference at baseline) row for 'Cingulate gyrus L' with cluster size 33 and 'Cingulate gyrus R' with cluster size 31 are listed without Brodmann area labels in those rows, though BA 31 appears in the Precuneus/Posterior cingulate row above them.

The paper does not describe randomization of participants. The study appears to be a single-arm open-label study stratified by gender post-hoc. The trial registration (NCT02448602) may contain additional design details not described in the paper.
